Whenever in the course of time there occurs a decline of dharma,

The blessed seer Śrī Śuka, who is the form of Nanda's son,
will recite the Śrīmad Bhāgavata to you, without doubt.

Know indeed that to be the Bhāgavata: that speech which wells forth

By plunging into its infinity, only those—

2.6.d: त एव संति भो विप्रा ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवादयः .. 7 ..
2.6.m: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the others, O brahmins—are capable of conveying what they themselves desire.
And for the benefit of human beings whose mental faculties are limited,

Now the listeners who take refuge in stories of Śrī Viṣṇu are described:

The superior are celebrated as the cātaka bird, the swan, the parrot, the fish, and others;
the inferior are celebrated as the wolf, the bhūruṇḍa bird, the bull, the camel, and others.
He who, disregarding everything else, is vowed to hearing the scripture of Kṛṣṇa,
he is a cātaka, like the cātaka bird intent on the water released by a cloud.
A listener who extracts the essence from diverse scriptures is [like] a swan,
just as a swan [takes] pure milk from water that has blended with milk. // 13

2.6.m: Rājasika, sāttvika, tāmasika, and likewise nirguṇa:
the service of the Śrībhāgavata is to be known as fourfold. // 24
That which is [performed for] seven days like a sacrifice, with effort, in haste, with joy,
attended upon with many worships and the like, is the rājasika one. // 25

accompanied by forgetting and remembering—such service is tāmasika, and brings happiness. // 27

Whatever is apart from Śrī Kṛṣṇa is all designated as 'wealth'. // 38

2.6.s: kṛṣṇārthīti dhanārthīti śrotā vaktā dvidhā mataḥ ..
2.6.d: कृष्णार्थीति धनार्थीति श्रोता वक्ता द्विधा मतः ..
2.6.m: A listener or speaker is considered two-fold: one seeking Kṛṣṇa, and one seeking wealth.

2.6.s: yathā vaktā tathā śrotā tatra saukhyaṃ vivarddhate .. 39 ..
2.6.d: यथा वक्ता तथा श्रोता तत्र सौख्यं विवर्द्धते .. 39 ..
2.6.m: As the speaker is, so is the listener; there happiness increases. // 39
When there is a discrepancy between the two, a semblance of sentiment results in the loss of the fruit;
however, for those seeking Kṛṣṇa, perfection arises even after a delay. // 40
The perfection of one who seeks wealth depends upon the completeness of the ritual rule;
for one who seeks Kṛṣṇa, even if lacking merit, love alone is the supreme rule. // 41

2.6.s: āsamāpti sakāmena kartavyo hi vidhiḥ svayam ..
2.6.d: आसमाप्ति सकामेन कर्तव्यो हि विधिः स्वयम् ..
2.6.m: Until completion, the ritual rule must indeed be observed personally by one who has desires.

2.6.s: snāto nitya kriyāṃ kṛtvā prāśya pādodakaṃ hareḥ .. 42 ..
2.6.d: स्नातो नित्य क्रियां कृत्वा प्राश्य पादोदकं हरेः .. 42 ..
2.6.m: Having bathed, performed the daily rites, and tasted the foot-nectar of Hari, // 42
and having worshipped both the book and the guru with the proper offerings,
he should speak or listen to the Śrīmad Bhāgavata with joy. (43)
He should eat in silence, either on milk or on sacrificial fare (haviṣya);
he should observe celibacy, sleep on the ground, and avoid anger, greed, and the like. (44)

2.6.s: kathānte kīrtanaṃ nityaṃ samāptau jāgaraṃ caret ..
2.6.d: कथान्ते कीर्तनं नित्यं समाप्तौ जागरं चरेत् ..
2.6.m: At the end of the recitation, he should always perform chanting (kīrtana); at its conclusion, he should keep a night-vigil.
Having fed the brahmins, he should please them with sacrificial gifts. (45)

2.6.s: gurave vastrabhūṣādi dattvā gāṃ ca samarpayet ..
2.6.d: गुरवे वस्त्रभूषादि दत्त्वा गां च समर्पयेत् ..
2.6.m: Having given garments, ornaments, and the like to the guru, he should also offer a cow.

2.6.s: evaṃ kṛte vidhāne tu labhate vāñchitaṃ phalam .. 46 ..
2.6.d: एवं कृते विधाने तु लभते वाञ्छितं फलम् .. 46 ..
2.6.m: When the procedure is thus performed, he obtains the desired fruit: (46)
a wife, a house, sons, kingship, wealth, and whatever else is desired.
However, acting with desire is not appropriate here; it is a mockery. (47)
It brings about the attainment of Kṛṣṇa, bestowing the fruit of eternal bliss of divine love;
the scripture Śrīmad Bhāgavata was spoken in the Kali [age] by the parrot-like Śuka. (48)

2.6.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīmadbhāgavatamāhātmye caturtho'dhyāyaḥ .. 4 ..
2.6.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे श्रीमद्भागवतमाहात्म्ये चतुर्थोऽध्यायः .. 4 ..
2.6.m: Thus ends the fourth chapter in the Śrīmadbhāgavatamāhātmya, in the second, Vaiṣṇava section of the venerable Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of eighty-one thousand [verses]. (4)

2.6.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇe dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrībhāgavatamahāpurāṇamāhātmyaṃ samāptam .. 2-6..
2.6.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराणे द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे श्रीभागवतमहापुराणमाहात्म्यं समाप्तम् .. 2-6..
2.6.m: Thus ends the Śrībhāgavatamahāpurāṇamāhātmya in the second, Vaiṣṇava section of the venerable Skanda Mahāpurāṇa. (2.6)
Now begins the sixth [sub-section], the Bhāgavatamāhātmya, in the Vaiṣṇava section. (2.6)

Chapter 1: In the dialogue between Sūta and Śaunaka, the inquiry of King Ambarīṣa to Nārada desiring to know the Vaiṣṇava duties and other virtues; Nārada's praise of the month of Vaiśākha, and the greatness of the ritual ablution in Vaiśākha.
Chapter 2: Praise of Vaiśākha; thereafter the topic of fault in not performing the vows of the month of Vaiśākha; praise of vows; the gift of water-booths in Vaiśākha; praise of the gifts of fans, umbrellas, and footwear; and praise of the gift of food.
Chapter 3: The gift of beds, blankets, garments, camphor, flowers, saffron, sandal, gorocana, betel, fruits, and the like; the construction of rest pavilions; praise of wells, ponds, and gardens; description of the seven items equivalent to a son in the absence of a son; the greatness of the gift of betel, buttermilk, curds, rice, ghee, jaggery, sugarcanes, sugarcane juice, and sweet drinks.

अध्यायः 4 वैशाखव्रतिनां वर्ज्यपदार्थाः, गृहस्नाने दुष्टफूलम्, व्रताकरणे दोषः, नदीसप्तगंगादेवखातवापीषु स्नानं दानं च, मधुसूदनप्राथनार्घ्यदानपूजनादिकम्.

2.6.m:
Chapter 4: Items to be avoided by those observing the Vaiśākha vow; the evil result of bathing at home; the fault in not performing vows; ritual ablution and gift-giving in rivers, the seven Gaṅgās, divine waters, and stepwells; prayer, offering of water (arghya), and worship to Madhusūdana.
Chapter 5: Explanation of the excellence of the month of Vaiśākha with reasons.
Chapter 6: Recital of the greatness of giving water in the month of Vaiśākha; the story of King Hemāṅgada on that subject—his birth in an animal womb due to not giving water in the month of Vaiśākha; his liberation through Śrutadeva after having become a lizard in the palace of the king of Mithilā.
Chapter 7: Having seen that wonder, the amazed King of Mithilā questions Śrutadeva, who recounts the greatness of gifts of water and other offerings in the month of Vaiśākha; the recounting of the account of his own father on that subject.
Chapter 8: Śrutadeva, questioned by the King of Mithilā, narrates the legend of Kākutstha, son of Ikṣvāku, concerning the greatness of Vaiśākha by means of the dialogue between Īśvara and Pārvatī.
Chapter 9: The brāhmaṇa Śrutakīrti, questioned by the King of Mithilā, recounts the birth of Kumāra; and praise of the religious duties of Vaiśākha.

2.6.s:
adhyāyaḥ 10 aśūnyavratakathanam, vaiśākhamāse chatradānādipraśaṃsā
adhyāyaḥ 11 maithilanṛpeṇa vaiśākhadharmaprasiddhikaraṇam, tena sarvajanānāṃ sadgatiprāptyā narakāṇāṃ śūnyatayā khinnasya yamasya brahmasamīpe gamanam
adhyāyaḥ 12 brahmaṇe yamena svaduḥkhanivedanam
adhyāyaḥ 13 vaiśākhamāhātmyakathanapūrvakaṃ brahmaṇā yamasya samādhānakaraṇam, tathāpi khedayuktena yamena sākaṃ brahmaṇo viṣṇusamīpe gamanam, viṣṇunā yamāya varapradānam, tatra vaiśākhadharmāṇāṃ praśaṃsā
adhyāyaḥ 14 vaiśākhasnānapraśaṃsā,vaiśākhamāhātmyakathāśravaṇapraśaṃsā,tatra karmaniṣṭhataponiṣṭhadvijakathā
adhyāyaḥ 15 pañcāladeśādhipasya puruyaśaso nṛpasya vaiśākhadharmācaraṇātsvarājyaprāptiḥ
adhyāyaḥ 16 atha puruyaśasā'kṣayyatṛtīyāyāṃ viṣṇoḥ stutikaraṇam, viṣṇukṛpayā ca tasya sāyujyamuktiprāptiḥ
2.6.d:
अध्यायः 10 अशून्यव्रतकथनम्, वैशाखमासे छत्रदानादिप्रशंसा
अध्यायः 11 मैथिलनृपेण वैशाखधर्मप्रसिद्धिकरणम्, तेन सर्वजनानां सद्गतिप्राप्त्या नरकाणां शून्यतया खिन्नस्य यमस्य ब्रह्मसमीपे गमनम्
अध्यायः 12 ब्रह्मणे यमेन स्वदुःखनिवेदनम्
अध्यायः 13 वैशाखमाहात्म्यकथनपूर्वकं ब्रह्मणा यमस्य समाधानकरणम्, तथापि खेदयुक्तेन यमेन साकं ब्रह्मणो विष्णुसमीपे गमनम्, विष्णुना यमाय वरप्रदानम्, तत्र वैशाखधर्माणां प्रशंसा
अध्यायः 14 वैशाखस्नानप्रशंसा,वैशाखमाहात्म्यकथाश्रवणप्रशंसा,तत्र कर्मनिष्ठतपोनिष्ठद्विजकथा
अध्यायः 15 पञ्चालदेशाधिपस्य पुरुयशसो नृपस्य वैशाखधर्माचरणात्स्वराज्यप्राप्तिः
अध्यायः 16 अथ पुरुयशसाऽक्षय्यतृतीयायां विष्णोः स्तुतिकरणम्, विष्णुकृपया च तस्य सायुज्यमुक्तिप्राप्तिः
2.6.m:
Chapter 10: Recital of the vow of Aśūnya; praise of gifts such as umbrellas in the month of Vaiśākha.
Chapter 11: The King of Mithilā makes the religious duties of Vaiśākha renowned; Yama, grieving due to the emptiness of the hells because all people attain a good rebirth thereby, approaches Brahmā.
Chapter 12: Yama's representation of his distress to Brahmā.
Chapter 13: Brahmā comforts Yama through explaining the greatness of Vaiśākha; nevertheless, Brahmā goes to Viṣṇu along with the grieving Yama; Viṣṇu grants a boon to Yama; praise of the religious duties of Vaiśākha therein.
Chapter 14: Praise of ritual ablution in Vaiśākha, praise of listening to the account of the Vaiśākha-māhātmya, and therein the story of the two brahmins dedicated to ritual works and dedicated to austerity.
Chapter 15: King Puruyaśas, ruler of the Pañcāla country, regains his kingdom through observing the duties of Vaiśākha.
Chapter 16: Now, the praise of Viṣṇu by Puruyaśas on Akṣayya-tṛtīyā, and his attainment of liberation by merging [into the Lord] through the grace of Viṣṇu.

2.6.s:
adhyāyaḥ 17 vaiśākhadharmakathanopakrama upānaddānaprasaṅgena śaṅkhanāmakadvijakathānakam, tatra śaṅkhanāmakadvijena vyādhāya vaiśākhadharmakathanaprasaṅgena dantilakohalamuktiprāptivṛttāṃtakathanam
adhyāyaḥ 18 vyādhasya pūrvajanmavṛttāntakathanama
adhyāyaḥ 19 brahmaśavdapratipādanapūrvakaṃ sarvadevāpekṣayāḥ prāṇasya mukhyatvakathanam ,prāṇadevasya mahattvalope kaṇvaśāpapratipādanam, tvaṃ gurudrohī bhaveti kaṇvaṃ prati prāṇavāyunā śāpapradānam
adhyāyaḥ 20 sattvādibhirguṇairjīvānāṃ tadanurūpajanmakarmādiphalaprāptikathanam, pralayavarṇanam vyūhāvatārakarmanirūpaṇam, dharmabhedanirūpaṇapūrvakaṃ bhagavadbhaktalakṣaṇanirūpaṇam, vaiśākhamāsadharmanirūpaṇam
2.6.d:
अध्यायः 17 वैशाखधर्मकथनोपक्रम उपानद्दानप्रसङ्गेन शङ्खनामकद्विजकथानकम्, तत्र शङ्खनामकद्विजेन व्याधाय वैशाखधर्मकथनप्रसङ्गेन दन्तिलकोहलमुक्तिप्राप्तिवृत्तांतकथनम्
अध्यायः 18 व्याधस्य पूर्वजन्मवृत्तान्तकथनम
अध्यायः 19 ब्रह्मशव्दप्रतिपादनपूर्वकं सर्वदेवापेक्षयाः प्राणस्य मुख्यत्वकथनम् ,प्राणदेवस्य महत्त्वलोपे कण्वशापप्रतिपादनम्, त्वं गुरुद्रोही भवेति कण्वं प्रति प्राणवायुना शापप्रदानम्
अध्यायः 20 सत्त्वादिभिर्गुणैर्जीवानां तदनुरूपजन्मकर्मादिफलप्राप्तिकथनम्, प्रलयवर्णनम् व्यूहावतारकर्मनिरूपणम्, धर्मभेदनिरूपणपूर्वकं भगवद्भक्तलक्षणनिरूपणम्, वैशाखमासधर्मनिरूपणम्
2.6.m:
Chapter 17: In the commencement of declaring the duties of Vaiśākha, the tale of the brahmin named Śaṅkha in connection with the gift of sandals, and therein the account of the attainment of liberation by Dantila and Kohala in connection with the exposition of the duties of Vaiśākha by the brahmin named Śaṅkha to a hunter.
Chapter 18: The account of the previous birth of the hunter.
Chapter 19: The declaration of the primacy of Prāṇa above all deities preceded by the exposition of the word 'brahman'; the declaration of the curse of Kaṇva upon the diminishment of the greatness of the god Prāṇa; the pronouncement of the curse by the breath-wind Prāṇa upon Kaṇva: 'Be one who betrays his guru!'
Chapter 20: The account of living beings obtaining the fruits of births, actions, and so forth in accordance with the qualities such as sattva; description of cosmic dissolution; determination of the acts of the emanations and incarnations; determination of the characteristics of a devotee of the Lord preceded by the determination of the varieties of duties; determination of the duties of the month of Vaiśākha.

2.6.s:
adhyāyaḥ 21 vaiśākhamāsamāhātmyaśravaṇena sarpasya muktiḥ, tasyaiva pūrvajanmavṛttāntakathanam, śaṃkhavyādhasaṃvāde vyādhasya janmāntare vālmīkarṣitvaprāptikathanam
adhyāyaḥ 22 vaiśākhasthitithimāhātmyavarṇanam, kalidharmanirūpaṇam
adhyāyaḥ 23 akṣayyatṛtīyāmāhātmyam
adhyāyaḥ 24 vaiśākhaśukladvādaśīmāhātmyam, kāśmīradeśasthadevadvijakathā
adhyāyaḥ 25 vaiśākhaśuklatrayodaśī caturdaśī-pūrṇiṃmā tithīnāṃ māhātmyavarṇanam, vaiśākhamāhātmyaśravaṇaphalavarṇanam
viṣayānukramaṇikā
2.6.d:
अध्यायः 21 वैशाखमासमाहात्म्यश्रवणेन सर्पस्य मुक्तिः, तस्यैव पूर्वजन्मवृत्तान्तकथनम्, शंखव्याधसंवादे व्याधस्य जन्मान्तरे वाल्मीकर्षित्वप्राप्तिकथनम्
अध्यायः 22 वैशाखस्थितिथिमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, कलिधर्मनिरूपणम्
अध्यायः 23 अक्षय्यतृतीयामाहात्म्यम्
अध्यायः 24 वैशाखशुक्लद्वादशीमाहात्म्यम्, काश्मीरदेशस्थदेवद्विजकथा
अध्यायः 25 वैशाखशुक्लत्रयोदशी चतुर्दशी-पूर्णिंमा तिथीनां माहात्म्यवर्णनम्, वैशाखमाहात्म्यश्रवणफलवर्णनम्
विषयानुक्रमणिका
2.6.m:
Chapter 21: The liberation of a snake by hearing the māhātmya of the month of Vaiśākha; the narration of its previous birth; in the dialogue of Śaṅkha and the hunter, the narration of the hunter attaining the status of the seer Vālmīki in another birth.
Chapter 22: Description of the māhātmya of the lunar days occurring in Vaiśākha; determination of the duties of the Kali age.
Chapter 23: The māhātmya of Akṣayya-tṛtīyā.
Chapter 24: The māhātmya of the bright twelfth lunar day of Vaiśākha; the story of Devadvija dwelling in the Kaśmīra country.
Chapter 25: Description of the māhātmya of the thirteenth, fourteenth, and full moon lunar days of the bright fortnight of Vaiśākha; description of the fruit of listening to the Vaiśākha-māhātmya.
